sections.title: 3. Health Grammar: Modals of Advice and Obligation
sections.description: Using modal verbs to give health recommendations and express necessity.

points.title: Should/Ought to for Advice
points.function: To give recommendations or suggestions for better health
examples: People ought to exercise regularly for good health.

points.title: Must/Have to for Obligation
points.function: To express necessity or strong recommendation in health contexts
examples: Patients must follow the prescribed treatment.
You have to make an appointment before seeing the specialist.

points.title: Need to for Necessity
points.function: To express what is necessary for health and wellbeing
examples: We need to maintain a balanced diet.
You need to get enough sleep to recover properly.

rows: You should reduce your sugar intake.
Patients must take medication as prescribed.
We need to stay hydrated during exercise.

tip.title: Pro-Tip: Modal Nuance
tip.text: Use "should" for general advice, "must" for medical necessity, and "need to" for personal health requirements.

sections.title: Health Vocabulary Practice
sections.description: Choose the best word or phrase to complete each health sentence.

questions.prompt: "A ________ considers the whole person - body, mind, and spirit - in treatment."
questions.explanation: A holistic approach considers connected physical, mental and social factors rather than treating one symptom in isolation.

questions.prompt: "________ focuses on preventing diseases rather than treating them after they occur."
questions.explanation: Preventive care acts before illness develops; reactive treatment and emergency response happen after a problem appears.

questions.prompt: "Maintaining a healthy ________ is essential for reducing stress and increasing productivity."
questions.explanation: Work-life balance describes a sustainable division between employment and personal life, matching the stress context.

questions.prompt: "________ involves techniques that encourage awareness of the present moment without judgment."
questions.explanation: Mindfulness practice trains non-judgmental awareness of the present moment; the other activities do not define that process.

questions.prompt: "A ________ provides all necessary nutrients for good health and wellbeing."
questions.explanation: A nutritious diet supplies the range of nutrients the body needs; fast food and a merely strict diet do not guarantee this.

questions.prompt: "Following a ________ helps ensure consistent health benefits from physical activity."
questions.explanation: A regular exercise routine provides repeated, planned activity; random or occasional activity does not ensure consistency.

questions.prompt: "________ is more formal than 'doctor' and is often used in professional healthcare contexts."
questions.explanation: Physician is the formal professional term for a medical doctor; healer and nurse refer to different roles.

questions.prompt: "If you feel ________, it's important to rest and recover properly."
questions.explanation: Exhausted means extremely tired and therefore fits the advice to rest; happy and excited do not indicate physical depletion.

questions.prompt: "________ foods provide essential vitamins and minerals without excessive calories."
questions.explanation: Nutritious describes food rich in useful nutrients; expensive and tasty describe price or flavour, not nutritional value.

questions.prompt: "________ refers to measures taken to avoid health problems before they occur."
questions.explanation: Prevention means action taken to stop a problem before it occurs; treatment and medication respond to an existing condition.

sections.title: Listening: The Habit Change Myth
sections.description: Listen to an expert distinguish popular claims from evidence-based advice.

audio.transcript: People often ask how many days it takes to form a healthy habit, as though there were a universal deadline. The popular answer is twenty-one days, but behaviour research shows much wider variation. A simple action, such as drinking water after breakfast, may become automatic relatively quickly. A demanding routine, such as exercising after a long workday, usually takes longer and is more sensitive to disruption. The useful question is therefore not, when will this become effortless, but, how can I make the desired action easier to repeat? Context matters. A stable cue, a convenient environment and a realistic minimum version of the behaviour all reduce friction. Someone aiming to walk daily might define success as ten minutes rather than an hour. On a good day, they can continue; on a difficult day, they can still preserve the pattern. Missing one occasion is rarely the problem. The greater risk is interpreting one interruption as evidence of failure and abandoning the habit completely. Tracking can help, but only if the measure supports the behaviour. Step counts, for example, are useful when they encourage movement, not when they create anxiety. Sustainable health habits are built through repeated opportunities, flexible expectations and an environment that makes the healthier choice more likely.

gistQuestions.prompt: Which idea does the expert challenge?
options: Every habit forms within a fixed number of days
gistQuestions.explanation: The expert rejects a universal habit-formation deadline.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why does the expert recommend a minimum version of a habit?
options: It preserves repetition on difficult days
It removes the need for goals
detailQuestions.explanation: A small minimum makes the pattern easier to maintain.
The expert cautions against measures that create anxiety.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: Listen for contrasts between the popular claim, the research finding and the practical recommendation.

sections.title: Writing Part 4: Health Advice
sections.description: Write a short formal response using the vocabulary from this lesson.

prompt.situation: Your friend has been feeling stressed and tired due to their busy schedule. Write a short email (80-140 words) giving them health advice. Include suggestions about work-life balance, exercise, and diet. Use at least 5 vocabulary words from this lesson.
prompt.referenceAnswer: Dear Friend, I'm sorry to hear you've been feeling stressed and exhausted. You should consider adopting a more holistic approach to your wellbeing. It's essential to maintain a healthy work-life balance to prevent burnout. You ought to incorporate a regular exercise routine into your weekly schedule, even if it's just a 20-minute walk. Additionally, try to follow a more nutritious diet with plenty of fruits and vegetables. Remember, preventive care is always better than treating health problems after they develop. Please take care of yourself and don't hesitate to consult a healthcare professional if you continue feeling unwell.

tip.title: B2 Writing Tip
tip.text: Use modal verbs (should, ought to, must) appropriately to give advice. Vary your sentence structures to make your writing more engaging.
